Help and security

A clear path from first connection to verified copy.

Vericopy is a local SSH file-transfer application. It checks the server identity, copies through SFTP, reads the remote file back, and verifies its SHA-256 digest.

01

Choose a source

Select one file or a folder. Folder transfers require Recursive.

02

Name the destination

Use user@host:/absolute/path. Include the SSH account explicitly.

03

Choose authentication

Use your SSH agent or key when available, or enter a one-time password.

04

Review and transfer

Confirm the host, path, policy, and options before Vericopy connects.

Recommended

SSH key or agent

An SSH agent keeps the private-key operation outside Vericopy. Load your key into the operating system’s SSH agent, or choose an unencrypted private-key file.

  • Leave Private key empty to try the agent and standard key locations.
  • For an encrypted key, load it into the agent first.
  • Saving a session stores the key path, never the key contents.

Easiest first connection

One-time SSH password

Choose password authentication when the server account permits it. The password is handed directly to the native SSH connection and is not added to saved sessions or transfer history.

  • Vericopy clears the visible field as the transfer starts.
  • The password still exists briefly in application memory while authenticating.
  • Host-key verification remains mandatory.
  • Keyboard-interactive and multi-factor prompts are not handled by this mode.

Required for every connection

Verify the server before sending credentials

known_hosts binds the server name to its public host key. Obtain the fingerprint from the server administrator or another trusted channel, compare it independently, and only then add it to your local known_hosts file. Vericopy stops on unknown or changed keys and offers no bypass.

Transfer manager

Queue work, then minimize Vericopy.

Each reviewed request becomes a separate transfer job. Up to two jobs run at once and additional work waits in order. Minimized windows keep transferring. Closing Vericopy while work is active asks whether to keep it open or quit and interrupt safely.

  • Canceling keeps compatible partial state so a later retry can resume.
  • Jobs restored after restart wait for an explicit retry.
  • Password jobs require the password again because Vericopy never stores it.

What Vericopy protects

Your review is part of the security model.

Always

Strict host verification, native SFTP, safe resume checks, SHA-256 readback, and explicit destination permissions.

Never

Password persistence, password logging, telemetry, silent host-key acceptance, or shell interpolation of file paths.
